poems.text: The sparrow is sorry for the peacock at the burden of its tail.

poems.title: Stray Birds 59: Never be afraid of the moments
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Never be afraid of the moments—thus sings the voice of the everlasting.

poems.title: Stray Birds 60: The hurricane seeks the shortest road by the
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The hurricane seeks the shortest road by the no-road, and suddenly ends its search in the Nowhere.

poems.title: Stray Birds 61: Take my wine in my own cup
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
Take my wine in my own cup, friend.
It loses its wreath of foam when poured into that of others.

poems.title: Stray Birds 62: The Perfect decks itself in beauty for the
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The Perfect decks itself in beauty for the love of the Imperfect.

poems.title: Stray Birds 63: God says to man
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: God says to man, "I heal you therefore I hurt, love you therefore punish."

poems.title: Stray Birds 64: Thank the flame for its light
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Thank the flame for its light, but do not forget the lampholder standing in the shade with constancy of patience.

poems.title: Stray Birds 65: Tiny grass
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Tiny grass, your steps are small, but you possess the earth under your tread.

poems.title: Stray Birds 66: The infant flower opens its bud and cries
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The infant flower opens its bud and cries, "Dear World, please do not fade."

poems.title: Stray Birds 67: God grows weary of great kingdoms
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: God grows weary of great kingdoms, but never of little flowers.

poems.title: Stray Birds 68: Wrong cannot afford defeat but Right can
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Wrong cannot afford defeat but Right can.

poems.title: Stray Birds 69: "I give my whole water in joy," sings
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: "I give my whole water in joy," sings the waterfall, "though little of it is enough for the thirsty."

poems.title: Stray Birds 70: Where is the fountain that throws up these
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Where is the fountain that throws up these flowers in a ceaseless outbreak of ecstasy?

poems.title: Stray Birds 71: The woodcutter's axe begged for its handle from
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
The woodcutter's axe begged for its handle from the tree.
The tree gave it.

poems.title: Stray Birds 72: In my solitude of heart I feel the
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: In my solitude of heart I feel the sigh of this widowed evening veiled with mist and rain.

poems.title: Stray Birds 73: Chastity is a wealth that comes from abundance
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Chastity is a wealth that comes from abundance of love.

poems.title: Stray Birds 74: The mist
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The mist, like love, plays upon the heart of the hills and brings out surprises of beauty.

poems.title: Stray Birds 75: We read the world wrong and say that
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: We read the world wrong and say that it deceives us.

poems.title: Stray Birds 76: The poet wind is out over the sea
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The poet wind is out over the sea and the forest to seek his own voice.

poems.title: Stray Birds 77: Every child comes with the message that God
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Every child comes with the message that God is not yet discouraged of man.

poems.title: Stray Birds 78: The grass seeks her crowd in the earth
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
The grass seeks her crowd in the earth.
The tree seeks his solitude of the sky.

poems.title: Stray Birds 79: Man barricades against himself
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Man barricades against himself.

poems.title: Stray Birds 80: Your voice
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Your voice, my friend, wanders in my heart, like the muffled sound of the sea among these listening pines.

poems.title: Stray Birds 81: What is this unseen flame of darkness whose
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: What is this unseen flame of darkness whose sparks are the stars?

poems.title: Stray Birds 82: Let life be beautiful like summer flowers and
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Let life be beautiful like summer flowers and death like autumn leaves.

poems.title: Stray Birds 83: He who wants to do good knocks at
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: He who wants to do good knocks at the gate; he who loves finds the gate open.

poems.title: Stray Birds 84: In death the many becomes one
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
In death the many becomes one; in life the one becomes many.
Religion will be one when God is dead.

poems.title: Stray Birds 85: The artist is the lover of Nature
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The artist is the lover of Nature, therefore he is her slave and her master.

poems.title: Stray Birds 86: "How far are you from me
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
"How far are you from me, O Fruit?"

"I am hidden in your heart, O Flower."

poems.title: Stray Birds 87: This longing is for the one who is
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: This longing is for the one who is felt in the dark, but not seen in the day.

poems.title: Stray Birds 88: "You are the big drop of dew under
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: "You are the big drop of dew under the lotus leaf, I am the smaller one on its upper side," said the dewdrop to the lake.

poems.title: Stray Birds 89: The scabbard is content to be dull when
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The scabbard is content to be dull when it protects the keenness of the sword.

poems.title: Stray Birds 90: In darkness the One appears as uniform
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: In darkness the One appears as uniform; in the light the One appears as manifold.

poems.title: Stray Birds 91: The great earth makes herself hospitable with the
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The great earth makes herself hospitable with the help of the grass.

poems.title: Stray Birds 92: The birth and death of the leaves are
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The birth and death of the leaves are the rapid whirls of the eddy whose wider circles move slowly among stars.

poems.title: Stray Birds 93: Power said to the world
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
Power said to the world, "You are mine.

The world kept it prisoner on her throne.

Love said to the world, "I am thine."

The world gave it the freedom of her house.

poems.title: Stray Birds 94: The mist is like the earth's desire
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The mist is like the earth's desire.  It hides the sun for whom she cries.

poems.title: Stray Birds 95: Be still
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Be still, my heart, these great trees are prayers.

poems.title: Stray Birds 96: The noise of the moment scoffs at the
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The noise of the moment scoffs at the music of the Eternal.

poems.title: Stray Birds 97: I think of other ages that floated upon
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: I think of other ages that floated upon the stream of life and love and death and are forgotten, and I feel the freedom of passing away.

poems.title: Stray Birds 98: The sadness of my soul is her bride's
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
The sadness of my soul is her bride's veil.
It waits to be lifted in the night.

poems.title: Stray Birds 99: Death's stamp gives value to the coin of
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Death's stamp gives value to the coin of life; making it possible to buy with life what is truly precious.

poems.title: Stray Birds 100: The cloud stood humbly in a corner of
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
The cloud stood humbly in a corner of the sky.
The morning crowned it with splendour.

poems.title: Stray Birds 101: The dust receives insult and in return offers
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The dust receives insult and in return offers her flowers.

poems.title: Stray Birds 102: Do not linger to gather flowers to keep
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Do not linger to gather flowers to keep them, but walk on, for flowers will keep themselves blooming all your way.

poems.title: Stray Birds 103: Roots are the branches down in the earth
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
Roots are the branches down in the earth.
Branches are roots in the air.

poems.title: Stray Birds 104: The music of the far-away summer flutters around
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The music of the far-away summer flutters around the Autumn seeking its former nest.

poems.title: Stray Birds 105: Do not insult your friend by lending him
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Do not insult your friend by lending him merits from your own pocket.

poems.title: Stray Birds 106: The touch of the nameless days clings to
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The touch of the nameless days clings to my heart like mosses round the old tree.

poems.title: Stray Birds 107: The echo mocks her origin to prove she
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The echo mocks her origin to prove she is the original.

poems.title: Stray Birds 108: God is ashamed when the prosperous boasts of
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: God is ashamed when the prosperous boasts of His special favour.

poems.title: Stray Birds 109: I cast my own shadow upon my path
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: I cast my own shadow upon my path, because I have a lamp that has not been lighted.

poems.title: Stray Birds 110: Man goes into the noisy crowd to drown
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Man goes into the noisy crowd to drown his own clamour of silence.

poems.title: Stray Birds 111: That which ends in exhaustion is death
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: That which ends in exhaustion is death, but the perfect ending is in the endless.

poems.title: Stray Birds 112: The sun has his simple robe of light
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The sun has his simple robe of light.  The clouds are decked with gorgeousness.

poems.title: Stray Birds 113: The hills are like shouts of children who
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The hills are like shouts of children who raise their arms, trying to catch stars.

poems.title: Stray Birds 114: The road is lonely in its crowd for
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The road is lonely in its crowd for it is not loved.

poems.title: Stray Birds 115: The power that boasts of its mischiefs is
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The power that boasts of its mischiefs is laughed at by the yellow leaves that fall, and clouds that pass by.

poems.title: Stray Birds 116: The earth hums to me to-day in the
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The earth hums to me to-day in the sun, like a woman at her spinng, some ballad of the ancient time in a forgotten tongue.

poems.title: Stray Birds 117: The grass-blade is worth of the great world
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The grass-blade is worth of the great world where it grows.

poems.title: Stray Birds 118: Dream is a wife who must talk
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
Dream is a wife who must talk.
Sleep is a husband who silently suffers.

poems.title: Stray Birds 119: The night kisses the fading day whispering to
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The night kisses the fading day whispering to his ear, "I am death, your mother.  I am to give you fresh birth."

poems.title: Stray Birds 120: I feel
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: I feel, thy beauty, dark night, like that of the loved woman when she has put out the lamp.

poems.title: Stray Birds 121: I carry in my world that flourishes the
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: I carry in my world that flourishes the worlds that have failed.

poems.title: Stray Birds 122: Dear friend
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Dear friend, I feel the silence of your great thoughts of may a deepening eventide on this beach when I listen to these waves.

poems.title: Stray Birds 123: The bird thinks it is an act of
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The bird thinks it is an act of kindness to give the fish a lift in the air.

poems.title: Stray Birds 124: "In the moon thou sendest thy love letters
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
"In the moon thou sendest thy love letters to me," said the night to the sun.

"I leave my answers in tears upon the grass."

poems.title: Stray Birds 125: The Great is a born child
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The Great is a born child; when he dies he gives his great childhood to the world.

poems.title: Stray Birds 126: Not hammerstrokes
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Not hammerstrokes, but dance of the water sings the pebbles into perfection.

poems.title: Stray Birds 127: Bees sip honey from flowers and hum their
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
Bees sip honey from flowers and hum their thanks when they leave.
The gaudy butterfly is sure that the flowers owe thanks to him.

poems.title: Stray Birds 128: To be outspoken is easy when you do
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: To be outspoken is easy when you do not wait to speak the complete truth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 129: Asks the Possible to the Impossible
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
Asks the Possible to the Impossible, "Where is your dwelling place?"

"In the dreams of the impotent," comes the answer.

poems.title: Stray Birds 130: If you shut your door to all errors
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: If you shut your door to all errors truth will be shut out.

poems.title: Stray Birds 131: I hear some rustle of things behind my
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: I hear some rustle of things behind my sadness of heart,—I cannot see them.

poems.title: Stray Birds 132: Leisure in its activity is work
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
Leisure in its activity is work.
The stillness of the sea stirs in waves.

poems.title: Stray Birds 133: The leaf becomes flower when it loves
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
The leaf becomes flower when it loves.
The flower becomes fruit when it worships.

poems.title: Stray Birds 134: The roots below the earth claim no rewards
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The roots below the earth claim no rewards for making the branches fruitful.

poems.title: Stray Birds 135: This rainy evening the wind is restless
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
This rainy evening the wind is restless.
I look at the swaying branches and ponder over the greatness of all things.

poems.title: Stray Birds 136: Storm of midnight
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Storm of midnight, like a giant child awakened in the untimely dark, has begun to play and shout.

poems.title: Stray Birds 137: Thou raisest thy waves vainly to follow thy
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Thou raisest thy waves vainly to follow thy lover.  O sea, thou lonely bride of the storm.

poems.title: Stray Birds 138: "I am ashamed of my emptiness," said the
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
"I am ashamed of my emptiness," said the Word to the Work.
"I know how poor I am when I see you," said the Work to the Word.

poems.title: Stray Birds 139: Time is the wealth of change
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Time is the wealth of change, but the clock in its parody makes it mere change and no wealth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 140: Truth in her dress finds facts too tight
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
Truth in her dress finds facts too tight.
In fiction she moves with ease.

poems.title: Stray Birds 141: When I travelled to here and to there
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: When I travelled to here and to there, I was tired of thee, O Road, but now when thou leadest me to everywhere I am wedded to thee in love.

poems.title: Stray Birds 142: Let me think that there is one among
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Let me think that there is one among those stars that guides my life through the dark unknown.

poems.title: Stray Birds 143: Woman
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Woman, with the grace of your fingers you touched my things and order came out like music.

poems.title: Stray Birds 144: One sad voice has its nest among the
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
One sad voice has its nest among the ruins of the years.
It sings to me in the night,—"I loved you."

poems.title: Stray Birds 145: The flaming fire warns me off by its
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
The flaming fire warns me off by its own glow.
Save me from the dying embers hidden under ashes.

poems.title: Stray Birds 146: I have my stars in the sky
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: I have my stars in the sky, But oh for my little lamp unlit in my house.

poems.title: Stray Birds 147: The dust of the dead words clings to
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
The dust of the dead words clings to thee.
Wash thy soul with silence.

poems.title: Stray Birds 148: Gaps are left in life through which comes
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Gaps are left in life through which comes the sad music of death.

poems.title: Stray Birds 149: The world has opened its heart of light
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
The world has opened its heart of light in the morning.
Come out, my heart, with thy love to meet it.

poems.title: Stray Birds 150: My thoughts shimmer with these shimmering leaves and
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: My thoughts shimmer with these shimmering leaves and my heart sings with the touch of this sunlight; my life is glad to be floating with all things into the blue of space, into the dark of time.

poems.title: Stray Birds 151: God's great power is in the gentle breeze
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: God's great power is in the gentle breeze, not in the storm.

poems.title: Stray Birds 152: This is a dream in which things are
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
This is a dream in which things are all loose and they oppress.
I shall find them gathered in thee when I awake and shall be free.

poems.title: Stray Birds 153: "Who is there to take up my duties?"
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
"Who is there to take up my duties?"  asked the setting sun.

"I shall do what I can, my Master," said the earthen lamp.

poems.title: Stray Birds 154: By plucking her petals you do not gather
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: By plucking her petals you do not gather the beauty of the flower.

poems.title: Stray Birds 155: Silence will carry your voice like the nest
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Silence will carry your voice like the nest that holds the sleeping birds.

poems.title: Stray Birds 156: The Great walks with the Small without fear
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
The Great walks with the Small without fear.
The Middling keeps aloof.

poems.title: Stray Birds 157: The night opens the flowers in secret and
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The night opens the flowers in secret and allows the day to get thanks.

poems.title: Stray Birds 158: Power takes as ingratitude the writhings of its
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Power takes as ingratitude the writhings of its victims.

poems.title: Stray Birds 159: When we rejoice in our fulness
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: When we rejoice in our fulness, then we can part with our fruits with joy.

poems.title: Stray Birds 160: The raindrops kissed the earth and whispered
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The raindrops kissed the earth and whispered,—"We are thy homesick children, mother, come back to thee from the heaven."

poems.title: Stray Birds 161: The cobweb pretends to catch dew-drops and catches
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The cobweb pretends to catch dew-drops and catches flies.

poems.title: Stray Birds 162: Love
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Love!  when you come with the burning lamp of pain in your hand, I can see your face and know you as bliss.

poems.title: Stray Birds 163: "The learned say that your lights will one
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
"The learned say that your lights will one day be no more."  said the firefly to the stars.

The stars made no answer.

poems.title: Stray Birds 164: In the dusk of the evening the bird
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: In the dusk of the evening the bird of some early dawn comes to the nest of my silence.

poems.title: Stray Birds 165: Thoughts pass in my mind like flocks of
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
Thoughts pass in my mind like flocks of ducks in the sky.
I hear the voice of their wings.

poems.title: Stray Birds 166: The canal loves to think that rivers exist
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The canal loves to think that rivers exist solely to supply it with water.

poems.title: Stray Birds 167: The world has kissed my soul with its
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The world has kissed my soul with its pain, asking for its return in songs.

poems.title: Stray Birds 168: That which oppresses me
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: That which oppresses me, is it my soul trying to come out in the open, or the soul of the world knocking at my heart for its entrance?

poems.title: Stray Birds 169: Thought feeds itself with its own words and
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Thought feeds itself with its own words and grows.

poems.title: Stray Birds 170: I have dipped the vessel of my heart
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: I have dipped the vessel of my heart into this silent hour; it has filled with love.

poems.title: Stray Birds 171: Either you have work or you have not
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
Either you have work or you have not.
When you have to say, "Let us do something," then begins mischief.

poems.title: Stray Birds 172: The sunflower blushed to own the nameless flower
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
The sunflower blushed to own the nameless flower as her kin.
The sun rose and smiled on it, saying, "Are you well, my darling?"

poems.title: Stray Birds 173: "Who drives me forward like fate?" "The Myself
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
"Who drives me forward like fate?"

"The Myself striding on my back."

poems.title: Stray Birds 174: The clouds fill the watercups of the river
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The clouds fill the watercups of the river, hiding themselves in the distant hills.

poems.title: Stray Birds 175: I spill water from my water jar as
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: I spill water from my water jar as I walk on my way, Very little remains for my home.

poems.title: Stray Birds 176: The water in a vessel is sparkling
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
The water in a vessel is sparkling; the water in the sea is dark.
The small truth has words that are clear; the great truth has great silence.

poems.title: Stray Birds 177: Your smile was the flowers of your own
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Your smile was the flowers of your own fields, your talk was the rustle of your own mountain pines, but your heart was the woman that we all know.

poems.title: Stray Birds 178: It is the little things that I leave
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: It is the little things that I leave behind for my loved ones,— great things are for everyone.

poems.title: Stray Birds 179: Woman
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Woman, thou hast encircled the world's heart with the depth of thy tears as the sea has the earth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 180: The sunshine greets me with a smile
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The sunshine greets me with a smile.  The rain, his sad sister, talks to my heart.

poems.title: Stray Birds 181: My flower of the day dropped its petals
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
My flower of the day dropped its petals forgotten.
In the evening it ripens into a golden fruit of memory.

poems.title: Stray Birds 182: I am like the road in the night
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: I am like the road in the night listening to the footfalls of its memories in silence.

poems.title: Stray Birds 183: The evening sky to me is like a
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The evening sky to me is like a window, and a lighted lamp, and a waiting behind it.

poems.title: Stray Birds 184: He who is too busy doing good finds
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: He who is too busy doing good finds no time to be good.

poems.title: Stray Birds 185: I am the autumn cloud
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: I am the autumn cloud, empty of rain, see my fulness in the field of ripened rice.

poems.title: Stray Birds 186: They hated and killed and men praised them
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
They hated and killed and men praised them.
But God in shame hastens to hide its memory under the green grass.

poems.title: Stray Birds 187: Toes are the fingers that have forsaken their
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Toes are the fingers that have forsaken their past.

poems.title: Stray Birds 188: Darkness travels towards light
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Darkness travels towards light, but blindness towards death.

poems.title: Stray Birds 189: The pet dog suspects the universe for scheming
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The pet dog suspects the universe for scheming to take its place.

poems.title: Stray Birds 190: Sit still my heart
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
Sit still my heart, do not raise your dust.
Let the world find its way to you.

poems.title: Stray Birds 191: The bow whispers to the arrow before it
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The bow whispers to the arrow before it speeds forth—"Your freedom is mine."

poems.title: Stray Birds 192: Woman
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Woman, in your laughter you have the music of the fountain of life.

poems.title: Stray Birds 193: A mind all logic is like a knife
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
A mind all logic is like a knife all blade.
It makes the hand bleed that uses it.

poems.title: Stray Birds 194: God loves man's lamp lights better than his
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: God loves man's lamp lights better than his own great stars.

poems.title: Stray Birds 195: This world is the world of wild storms
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: This world is the world of wild storms kept tame with the music of beauty.

poems.title: Stray Birds 196: "My heart is like the golden casket of
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: "My heart is like the golden casket of thy kiss," said the sunset cloud to the sun.

poems.title: Stray Birds 197: By touching you may kill
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: By touching you may kill, by keeping away you may possess.

poems.title: Stray Birds 198: The cricket's chirp and the patter of rain
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The cricket's chirp and the patter of rain come to me through the dark, like the rustle of dreams from my past youth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 199: "I have lost my dewdrop," cries the flower
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: "I have lost my dewdrop," cries the flower to the morning sky that has lost all its stars.

poems.title: Stray Birds 200: The burning log bursts in flame and cries
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The burning log bursts in flame and cries,—"This is my flower, my death."

poems.title: Stray Birds 201: The wasp thinks that the honey-hive of the
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
The wasp thinks that the honey-hive of the neighbouring bees is too small.
His neighbours ask him to build one still smaller.

poems.title: Stray Birds 202: "I cannot keep your waves," says the bank
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
"I cannot keep your waves," says the bank to the river.

"Let me keep your footprints in my heart."

poems.title: Stray Birds 203: The day
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The day, with the noise of this little earth, drowns the silence of all worlds.

poems.title: Stray Birds 204: The song feels the infinite in the air
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The song feels the infinite in the air, the picture in the earth, the poem in the air and the earth; For its words have meaning that walks and music that soars.

poems.title: Stray Birds 205: When the sun goes down to the West
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: When the sun goes down to the West, the East of his morning stands before him in silence.

poems.title: Stray Birds 206: Let me not put myself wrongly to my
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Let me not put myself wrongly to my world and set it against me.

poems.title: Stray Birds 207: Praise shames me
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Praise shames me, for I secretly beg for it.

poems.title: Stray Birds 208: Let my doing nothing when I have nothing
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Let my doing nothing when I have nothing to do become untroubled in its depth of peace like the evening in the seashore when the water is silent.

poems.title: Stray Birds 209: Maiden
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Maiden, your simplicity, like the blueness of the lake, reveals your depth of truth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 210: The best does not come alone
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The best does not come alone.  It comes with the company of the all.

poems.title: Stray Birds 211: God's right hand is gentle
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: God's right hand is gentle, but terrible is his left hand.

poems.title: Stray Birds 212: My evening came among the alien trees and
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: My evening came among the alien trees and spoke in a language which my morning stars did not know.

poems.title: Stray Birds 213: Night's darkness is a bag that bursts with
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Night's darkness is a bag that bursts with the gold of the dawn.

poems.title: Stray Birds 214: Our desire lends the colours of the rainbow
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Our desire lends the colours of the rainbow to the mere mists and vapours of life.

poems.title: Stray Birds 215: God waits to win back his own flowers
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: God waits to win back his own flowers as gifts from man's hands.

poems.title: Stray Birds 216: My sad thoughts tease me asking me their
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: My sad thoughts tease me asking me their own names.

poems.title: Stray Birds 217: The service of the fruit is precious
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The service of the fruit is precious, the service of the flower is sweet, but let my service be the service of the leaves in its shade of humble devotion.

poems.title: Stray Birds 218: My heart has spread its sails to the
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: My heart has spread its sails to the idle winds for the shadowy island of Anywhere.

poems.title: Stray Birds 219: Men are cruel
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Men are cruel, but Man is kind.

poems.title: Stray Birds 220: Make me thy cup and let my fulness
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Make me thy cup and let my fulness be for thee and for thine.

poems.title: Stray Birds 221: The storm is like the cry of some
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The storm is like the cry of some god in pain whose love the earth refuses.

poems.title: Stray Birds 222: The world does not leak because death is
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The world does not leak because death is not a crack.

poems.title: Stray Birds 223: Life has become richer by the love that
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Life has become richer by the love that has been lost.

poems.title: Stray Birds 224: My friend
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: My friend, your great heart shone with the sunrise of the East like the snowy summit of a lonely hill in the dawn.

poems.title: Stray Birds 225: The fountain of death makes the still water
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The fountain of death makes the still water of life play.

poems.title: Stray Birds 226: Those who have everything but thee
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Those who have everything but thee, my God, laugh at those who have nothing but thyself.

poems.title: Stray Birds 227: The movement of life has its rest in
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The movement of life has its rest in its own music.

poems.title: Stray Birds 228: Kicks only raise dust and not crops from
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Kicks only raise dust and not crops from the earth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 229: Our names are the light that glows on
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Our names are the light that glows on the sea waves at night and then dies without leaving its signature.

poems.title: Stray Birds 230: Let him only see the thorns who has
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Let him only see the thorns who has eyes to see the rose.

poems.title: Stray Birds 231: Set bird's wings with gold and it will
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Set bird's wings with gold and it will never again soar in the sky.

poems.title: Stray Birds 232: The same lotus of our clime blooms here
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The same lotus of our clime blooms here in the alien water with the same sweetness, under another name.

poems.title: Stray Birds 233: In heart's perspective the distance looms large
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: In heart's perspective the distance looms large.

poems.title: Stray Birds 234: The moon has her light all over the
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The moon has her light all over the sky, her dark spots to herself.

poems.title: Stray Birds 235: Do not say
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Do not say, "It is morning," and dismiss it with a name of yesterday.  See it for the first time as a new-born child that has no name.

poems.title: Stray Birds 236: Smoke boasts to the sky
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Smoke boasts to the sky, and Ashes to the earth, that they are brothers to the fire.

poems.title: Stray Birds 237: The raindrop whispered to the jasmine
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
The raindrop whispered to the jasmine, "Keep me in your heart for ever."

The jasmine sighed, "Alas," and dropped to the ground.

poems.title: Stray Birds 238: Timid thoughts
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
Timid thoughts, do not be afraid of me.
I am a poet.

poems.title: Stray Birds 239: The dim silence of my mind seems filled
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The dim silence of my mind seems filled with crickets' chirp—the grey twilight of sound.

poems.title: Stray Birds 240: Rockets
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Rockets, your insult to the stars follows yourself back to the earth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 241: Thou hast led me through my crowded travels
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
Thou hast led me through my crowded travels of the day to my evening's loneliness.
I wait for its meaning through the stillness of the night.

poems.title: Stray Birds 242: This life is the crossing of a sea
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
This life is the crossing of a sea, where we meet in the same narrow ship.
In death we reach the shore and go to our different worlds.

poems.title: Stray Birds 243: The stream of truth flows through its channels
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The stream of truth flows through its channels of mistakes.

poems.title: Stray Birds 244: My heart is homesick to-day for the one
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: My heart is homesick to-day for the one sweet hour across the sea of time.

poems.title: Stray Birds 245: The bird-song is the echo of the morning
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The bird-song is the echo of the morning light back from the earth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 246: "Are you too proud to kiss me?" the
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: "Are you too proud to kiss me?"  the morning light asks the buttercup.

poems.title: Stray Birds 247: "How may I sing to thee and worship
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
"How may I sing to thee and worship, O Sun?"  asked the little flower.

"By the simple silence of thy purity," answered the sun.

poems.title: Stray Birds 248: Man is worse than an animal when he
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Man is worse than an animal when he is an animal.

poems.title: Stray Birds 249: Dark clouds become heaven's flowers when kissed by
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Dark clouds become heaven's flowers when kissed by light.

poems.title: Stray Birds 250: Let not the sword-blade mock its handle for
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Let not the sword-blade mock its handle for being blunt.

poems.title: Stray Birds 251: The night's silence
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The night's silence, like a deep lamp, is burning with the light of its milky way.

poems.title: Stray Birds 252: Around the sunny island of Life swells day
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Around the sunny island of Life swells day and night death's limitless song of the sea.

poems.title: Stray Birds 253: Is not this mountain like a flower
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Is not this mountain like a flower, with its petals of hills, drinking the sunlight?

poems.title: Stray Birds 254: The real with its meaning read wrong and
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The real with its meaning read wrong and emphasis misplaced is the unreal.

poems.title: Stray Birds 255: Find your beauty
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Find your beauty, my heart, from the world's movement, like the boat that has the grace of the wind and the water.

poems.title: Stray Birds 256: The eyes are not proud of their sight
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The eyes are not proud of their sight but of their eyeglasses.

poems.title: Stray Birds 257: I live in this little world of mine
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: I live in this little world of mine and am afraid to make it the least less.  Lift me into thy world and let me have the freedom gladly to lose my all.

poems.title: Stray Birds 258: The false can never grow into truth by
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The false can never grow into truth by growing in power.

poems.title: Stray Birds 259: My heart
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: My heart, with its lapping waves of song, longs to caress this green world of the sunny day.

poems.title: Stray Birds 260: Wayside grass
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Wayside grass, love the star, then your dreams will come out in flowers.

poems.title: Stray Birds 261: Let your music
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Let your music, like a sword, pierce the noise of the market to its heart.

poems.title: Stray Birds 262: The trembling leaves of this tree touch my
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The trembling leaves of this tree touch my heart like the fingers of an infant child.

poems.title: Stray Birds 263: This sadness of my soul is her bride's
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
This sadness of my soul is her bride's veil.
It waits to be lifted in the night.

poems.title: Stray Birds 264: The little flower lies in the dust
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
The little flower lies in the dust.
It sought the path of the butterfly.

poems.title: Stray Birds 265: I am in the world of the roads
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: I am in the world of the roads.  The night comes.  Open thy gate, thou world of the home.

poems.title: Stray Birds 266: I have sung the songs of thy day
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: I have sung the songs of thy day.  In the evening let me carry thy lamp through the stormy path.

poems.title: Stray Birds 267: I do not ask thee into the house
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
I do not ask thee into the house.
Come into my infinite loneliness, my Lover.

poems.title: Stray Birds 268: Death belongs to life as birth does
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Death belongs to life as birth does.  The walk is in the raising of the foot as in the laying of it down.

poems.title: Stray Birds 269: I have learnt the simple meaning of thy
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: I have learnt the simple meaning of thy whispers in flowers and sunshine—teach me to know thy words in pain and death.

poems.title: Stray Birds 270: The night's flower was late when the morning
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The night's flower was late when the morning kissed her, she shivered and sighed and dropped to the ground.

poems.title: Stray Birds 271: Through the sadness of all things I hear
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Through the sadness of all things I hear the crooning of the Eternal Mother.

poems.title: Stray Birds 272: I came to your shore as a stranger
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: I came to your shore as a stranger, I lived in your house as a guest, I leave your door as a friend, my earth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 273: Let my thoughts come to you
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Let my thoughts come to you, when I am gone, like the afterglow of sunset at the margin of starry silence.

poems.title: Stray Birds 274: Light in my heart the evening star of
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Light in my heart the evening star of rest and then let the night whisper to me of love.

poems.title: Stray Birds 275: I am a child in the dark
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
I am a child in the dark.
I stretch my hands through the coverlet of night for thee, Mother.

poems.title: Stray Birds 276: The day of work is done
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
The day of work is done.  Hide my face in your arms, Mother.
Let me dream.

poems.title: Stray Birds 277: The lamp of meeting burns long
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The lamp of meeting burns long; it goes out in a moment at the parting.

poems.title: Stray Birds 278: One word keep for me in thy silence
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: One word keep for me in thy silence, O World, when I am dead, "I have loved."

poems.title: Stray Birds 279: We live in this world when we love
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: We live in this world when we love it.

poems.title: Stray Birds 280: Let the dead have the immortality of fame
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Let the dead have the immortality of fame, but the living the immortality of love.

poems.title: Stray Birds 281: I have seen thee as the half-awakened child
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: I have seen thee as the half-awakened child sees his mother in the dusk of the dawn and then smiles and sleeps again.

poems.title: Stray Birds 282: I shall die again and again to know
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: I shall die again and again to know that life is inexhaustible.

poems.title: Stray Birds 283: While I was passing with the crowd in
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: While I was passing with the crowd in the road I saw thy smile from the balcony and I sang and forgot all noise.

poems.title: Stray Birds 284: Love is life in its fulness like the
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Love is life in its fulness like the cup with its wine.

poems.title: Stray Birds 285: They light their own lamps and sing their
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
They light their own lamps and sing their own words in their temples.
But the birds sing thy name in thine own morning light,—for thy name is joy.

poems.title: Stray Birds 286: Lead me in the centre of thy silence
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Lead me in the centre of thy silence to fill my heart with songs.

poems.title: Stray Birds 287: Let them live who choose in their own
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
Let them live who choose in their own hissing world of fireworks.
My heart longs for thy stars, my God.

poems.title: Stray Birds 288: Love's pain sang round my life like the
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Love's pain sang round my life like the unplumbed sea, and love's joy sang like birds in its flowering groves.

poems.title: Stray Birds 289: Put out the lamp when thou wishest
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
Put out the lamp when thou wishest.
I shall know thy darkness and shall love it.

poems.title: Stray Birds 290: When I stand before thee at the day's
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: When I stand before thee at the day's end thou shalt see my scars and know that I had my wounds and also my healing.

poems.title: Stray Birds 291: Some day I shall sing to thee in
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Some day I shall sing to thee in the sunrise of some other world, "I have seen thee before in the light of the earth, in the love of man."

poems.title: Stray Birds 292: Clouds come floating into my life from other
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Clouds come floating into my life from other days no longer to shed rain or usher storm but to give colour to my sunset sky.

poems.title: Stray Birds 293: Truth raises against itself the storm that scatters
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Truth raises against itself the storm that scatters its seeds broadcast.

poems.title: Stray Birds 294: The storm of the last night has crowned
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The storm of the last night has crowned this morning with golden peace.

poems.title: Stray Birds 295: Truth seems to come with its final word
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Truth seems to come with its final word; and the final word gives birth to its next.

poems.title: Stray Birds 296: Blessed is he whose fame does not outshine
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Blessed is he whose fame does not outshine his truth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 297: Sweetness of thy name fills my heart when
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Sweetness of thy name fills my heart when I forget mine—like thy morning sun when the mist is melted.

poems.title: Stray Birds 298: The silent night has the beauty of the
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The silent night has the beauty of the mother and the clamorous day of the child.

poems.title: Stray Birds 299: The world loved man when he smiled
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The world loved man when he smiled.  The world became afraid of him when he laughed.

poems.title: Stray Birds 300: God waits for man to regain his childhood
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: God waits for man to regain his childhood in wisdom.

poems.title: Stray Birds 301: Let me feel this world as thy love
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Let me feel this world as thy love taking form, then my love will help it.

poems.title: Stray Birds 302: Thy sunshine smiles upon the winter days of
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Thy sunshine smiles upon the winter days of my heart, never doubting of its spring flowers.

poems.title: Stray Birds 303: God kisses the finite in his love and
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: God kisses the finite in his love and man the infinite.

poems.title: Stray Birds 304: Thou crossest desert lands of barren years to
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Thou crossest desert lands of barren years to reach the moment of fulfilment.

poems.title: Stray Birds 305: God's silence ripens man's thoughts into speech
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: God's silence ripens man's thoughts into speech.

poems.title: Stray Birds 306: Thou wilt find
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Thou wilt find, Eternal Traveller, marks of thy footsteps across my songs.

poems.title: Stray Birds 307: Let me not shame thee
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Let me not shame thee, Father, who displayest thy glory in thy children.

poems.title: Stray Birds 308: Cheerless is the day
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Cheerless is the day, the light under frowning clouds is like a punished child with traces of tears on its pale cheeks, and the cry of the wind is like the cry of a wounded world.  But I know I am travelling to meet my Friend.

poems.title: Stray Birds 309: To-night there is a stir among the palm
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: To-night there is a stir among the palm leaves, a swell in the sea, Full Moon, like the heart throb of the world.  From what unknown sky hast thou carried in thy silence the aching secret of love?

poems.title: Stray Birds 310: I dream of a star
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: I dream of a star, an island of light, where I shall be born and in the depth of its quickening leisure my life will ripen its works like the ricefield in the autumn sun.

poems.title: Stray Birds 311: The smell of the wet earth in the
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The smell of the wet earth in the rain rises like a great chant of praise from the voiceless multitude of the insignificant.

poems.title: Stray Birds 312: That love can ever lose is a fact
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: That love can ever lose is a fact that we cannot accept as truth.

poems.title: Stray Birds 313: We shall know some day that death can
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: We shall know some day that death can never rob us of that which our soul has gained, for her gains are one with herself.

poems.title: Stray Birds 314: God comes to me in the dusk of
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: God comes to me in the dusk of my evening with the flowers from my past kept fresh in his basket.

poems.title: Stray Birds 315: When all the strings of my life will
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: When all the strings of my life will be tuned, my Master, then at every touch of thine will come out the music of love.

poems.title: Stray Birds 316: Let me live truly
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Let me live truly, my Lord, so that death to me become true.

poems.title: Stray Birds 317: Man's history is waiting in patience for the
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Man's history is waiting in patience for the triumph of the insulted man.

poems.title: Stray Birds 318: I feel thy gaze upon my heart this
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: I feel thy gaze upon my heart this moment like the sunny silence of the morning upon the lonely field whose harvest is over.

poems.title: Stray Birds 319: I long for the Island of Songs across
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: I long for the Island of Songs across this heaving Sea of Shouts.

poems.title: Stray Birds 320: The prelude of the night is commenced in
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: The prelude of the night is commenced in the music of the sunset, in its solemn hymn to the ineffable dark.

poems.title: Stray Birds 321: I have scaled the peak and found no
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: I have scaled the peak and found no shelter in fame's bleak and barren height.  Lead me, my Guide, before the light fades, into the valley of quiet where life's harvest mellows into golden wisdom.

poems.title: Stray Birds 322: Things look phantastic in this dimness of the
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
Things look phantastic in this dimness of the dusk—the spires whose bases are lost in the dark and tree tops like blots of ink.
I shall wait for the morning and wake up to see thy city in the light.

poems.title: Stray Birds 323: I have suffered and despaired and known death
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: I have suffered and despaired and known death and I am glad that I am in this great world.

poems.title: Stray Birds 324: There are tracts in my life that are
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: There are tracts in my life that are bare and silent.  They are the open spaces where my busy days had their light and air.

poems.title: Stray Birds 325: Release me from my unfulfilled past clinging to
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Release me from my unfulfilled past clinging to me from behind making death difficult.

poems.title: Stray Birds 326: Let this be my last word
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Let this be my last word, that I trust in thy love.

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 1: Bid me and I shall gather my fruits
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
Bid me and I shall gather my fruits to bring them in full baskets into your courtyard, though some are lost and some not ripe.

For the season grows heavy with its fulness, and there is a plaintive shepherd's pipe in the shade.

Bid me and I shall set sail on the river.

The March wind is fretful, fretting the languid waves into murmurs.

The garden has yielded its all, and in the weary hour of evening the call comes from your house on the shore in the sunset.

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 2: My life when young was like a flower
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
My life when young was like a flower—a flower that loosens a petal or two from her abundance and never feels the loss when the spring breeze comes to beg at her door.

Now at the end of youth my life is like a fruit, having nothing to spare, and waiting to offer herself completely with her full burden of sweetness.

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 3: Is summer's festival only for fresh blossoms and
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
Is summer's festival only for fresh blossoms and not also for withered leaves and faded flowers?

Is the song of the sea in tune only with the rising waves?

Does it not also sing with the waves that fall?

Jewels are woven into the carpet where stands my king, but there are patient clods waiting to be touched by his feet.

Few are the wise and the great who sit by my Master, but he has taken the foolish in his arms and made me his servant for ever.

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 4: I woke and found his letter with the
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
I woke and found his letter with the morning.

I do not know what it says, for I cannot read.

I shall leave the wise man alone with his books, I shall not trouble him, for who knows if he can read what the letter says.

Let me hold it to my forehead and press it to my heart.

When the night grows still and stars come out one by one I will spread it on my lap and stay silent.

The rustling leaves will read it aloud to me, the rushing stream will chant it, and the seven wise stars will sing it to me from the sky.

I cannot find what I seek, I cannot understand what I would learn; but this unread letter has lightened my burdens and turned my thoughts into songs.

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 5: A handful of dust could hide your signal
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
A handful of dust could hide your signal when I did not know its meaning.

Now that I am wiser I read it in all that hid it before.

It is painted in petals of flowers; waves flash it from their foam; hills hold it high on their summits.

I had my face turned from you, therefore I read the letters awry and knew not their meaning.

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 6: Where roads are made I lose my way
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
Where roads are made I lose my way.

In the wide water, in the blue sky there is no line of a track.

The pathway is hidden by the birds' wings, by the star-fires, by the flowers of the wayfaring seasons.

And I ask my heart if its blood carries the wisdom of the unseen way.

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 7: Alas
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
Alas, I cannot stay in the house, and home has become no home to me, for the eternal Stranger calls, he is going along the road.

The sound of his footfall knocks at my breast; it pains me!

The wind is up, the sea is moaning.  I leave all my cares and doubts to follow the homeless tide, for the Stranger calls me, he is going along the road.

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 8: Be ready to launch forth
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
Be ready to launch forth, my heart! and let those linger who must.

For your name has been called in the morning sky.

Wait for none!

The desire of the bud is for the night and dew, but the blown flower cries for the freedom of light.

Burst your sheath, my heart, and come forth!

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 9: When I lingered among my hoarded treasure I
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
When I lingered among my hoarded treasure I felt like a worm that feeds in the dark upon the fruit where it was born.

I leave this prison of decay.

I care not to haunt the mouldy stillness, for I go in search of everlasting youth; I throw away all that is not one with my life nor as light as my laughter.

I run through time and, O my heart, in your chariot dances the poet who sings while he wanders.

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 10: You took my hand and drew me to
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
You took my hand and drew me to your side, made me sit on the high seat before all men, till I became timid, unable to stir and walk my own way; doubting and debating at every step lest I should tread upon any thorn of their disfavour.

I am freed at last!

The blow has come, the drum of insult sounded, my seat is laid low in the dust.

My paths are open before me.

My wings are full of the desire of the sky.

I go to join the shooting stars of midnight, to plunge into the profound shadow.

I am like the storm-driven cloud of summer that, having cast off its crown of gold, hangs as a sword the thunderbolt upon a chain of lightning.

In desperate joy I run upon the dusty path of the despised; I draw near to your final welcome.

The child finds its mother when it leaves her womb.

When I am parted from you, thrown out from your household, I am free to see your face.

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 11: It decks me only to mock me
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
It decks me only to mock me, this jewelled chain of mine.

It bruises me when on my neck, it strangles me when I struggle to tear it off.

It grips my throat, it chokes my singing.

Could I but offer it to your hand, my Lord, I would be saved.

Take it from me, and in exchange bind me to you with a garland, for I am ashamed to stand before you with this jewelled chain on my neck.

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 12: Far below flowed the Jumna
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
Far below flowed the Jumna, swift and clear, above frowned the jutting bank.

Hills dark with the woods and scarred with the torrents were gathered around.

Govinda, the great Sikh teacher, sat on the rock reading scriptures, when Raghunath, his disciple, proud of his wealth, caine and bowed to him and said, "I have brought my poor present unworthy of your acceptance."

[Transcriber's note: In the above verse, the word 'caine' does not fit in, the word 'came' makes more sense]

Thus saying he displayed before the teacher a pair of gold bangles wrought with costly stones.

The master took up one of them, twirling it round his finger, and the diamonds darted shafts of light.

Suddenly it slipped from his hand and rolled down the bank into the water.

"Alas," screamed Raghunath, and jumped into the stream.

The teacher set his eyes upon his book, and the water held and hid what it stole and went its way.

The daylight faded when Raghunath came back to the teacher tired and dripping.

He panted and said, "I can still get it back if you show me where it fell."

The teacher took up the remaining bangle and throwing it into the water said, "It is there."

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 13: To move is to meet you every moment
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
To move is to meet you every moment, Fellow-traveller!

It is to sing to the falling of your feet.

He whom your breath touches does not glide by the shelter of the bank.

He spreads a reckless sail to the wind and rides the turbulent water.

He who throws his doors open and steps onward receives your greeting.

He does not stay to count his gain or to mourn his loss; his heart beats the drum for his march, for that is to march with you every step,

Fellow-traveller!

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 14: My portion of the best in this world
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
My portion of the best in this world will come from your hands: such was your promise.

Therefore your light glistens in my tears.

I fear to be led by others lest I miss you waiting in some road corner to be my guide.

I walk my own wilful way till my very folly tempts you to my door.

For I have your promise that my portion of the best in this world will come from your hands.

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 15: Your speech is simple
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
Your speech is simple, my Master, but not theirs who talk of you.

I understand the voice of your stars and the silence of your trees.

I know that my heart would open like a flower; that my life has filled itself at a hidden fountain.

Your songs, like birds from the lonely land of snow, are winging to build their nests in my heart against the warmth of its April, and I am content to wait for the merry season.

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 16: They knew the way and went to seek
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
They knew the way and went to seek you along the narrow lane, but I wandered abroad into the night for I was ignorant.

I was not schooled enough to be afraid of you in the dark, therefore I came upon your doorstep unaware.

The wise rebuked me and bade me be gone, for I had not come by the lane.

I turned away in doubt, but you held me fast, and their scolding became louder every day.

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 17: I brought out my earthen lamp from my
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
I brought out my earthen lamp from my house and cried, "Come, children, I will light your path!"

The night was still dark when I returned, leaving the road to its silence, crying, "Light me, O Fire! for my earthen lamp lies broken in the dust!"

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 18: No
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
No: it is not yours to open buds into blossoms.

Shake the bud, strike it; it is beyond your power to make it blossom.

Your touch soils it, you tear its petals to pieces and strew them in the dust.

But no colours appear, and no perfume.

Ah! it is not for you to open the bud into a blossom.

He who can open the bud does it so simply.

He gives it a glance, and the life-sap stirs through its veins.

At his breath the flower spreads its wings and flutters in the wind.

Colours flush out like heart-longings, the perfume betrays a sweet secret.

He who can open the bud does it so simply.

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 19: Sudâs
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Sudâs, the gardener, plucked from his tank the last lotus left by the ravage of winter and went to sell it to the king at the palace gate. There he met a traveller who said to him, "Ask your price for the last lotus, —I shall offer it to Lord Buddha." Sudâs said, "If you pay one golden mâshâ it will be yours. The traveller paid it. At that moment the king came out and he wished to buy the flower, for he was on his way to see Lord Buddha, and he thought, "It would be a fine thing to lay at his feet the lotus that bloomed in winter." When the gardener said he had been offered a golden mâshâ the king offered him ten, but the traveller doubled the price. The gardener, being greedy, imagined a greater gain from him for whose sake they were bidding. He bowed and said, "I cannot sell this lotus." In the hushed shade of the mango grove beyond the city wall Sudâs stood before Lord Buddha, on whose lips sat the silence of love and whose eyes beamed peace like the morning star of the dew-washed autumn. Sudâs looked in his face and put the lotus at his feet and bowed his head to the dust. Buddha smiled and asked, "What is your wish, my son?" Sudâs cried, "The least touch of your feet."

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 20: Make me thy poet
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
Make me thy poet, O Night, veiled Night!

There are some who have sat speechless for ages in thy shadow; let me utter their songs.

Take me up on thy chariot without wheels, running noiselessly from world to world, thou queen in the palace of time, thou darkly beautiful!

Many a questioning mind has stealthily entered thy courtyard and roamed through thy lampless house seeking for answers.

From many a heart, pierced with the arrow of joy from the hands of the Unknown, have burst forth glad chants, shaking the darkness to its foundation.

Those wakeful souls gaze in the starlight in wonder at the treasure they have suddenly found.

Make me their poet, O Night, the poet of thy fathomless silence.

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 21: I will meet one day the Life within
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
I will meet one day the Life within me, the joy that hides in my life, though the days perplex my path with their idle dust.

I have known it in glimpses, and its fitful breath has come upon me, making my thoughts fragrant for a while.

I will meet one day the Joy without me that dwells behind the screen of light—and will stand in the overflowing solitude where all things are seen as by their creator.

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 22: This autumn morning is tired with excess of
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
This autumn morning is tired with excess of light, and if your songs grow fitful and languid give me your flute awhile.

I shall but play with it as the whim takes me,—now take it on my lap, now touch it with my lips, now keep it by my side on the grass.

But in the solemn evening stillness I shall gather flowers, to deck it with wreaths, I shall fill it with fragrance; I shall worship it with the lighted lamp.

Then at night I shall come to you and give you back your flute.

You will play on it the music of midnight when the lonely crescent moon wanders among the stars.

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 23: The poet's mind floats and dances on the
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
The poet's mind floats and dances on the waves of life amidst the voices of wind and water.

Now when the sun has set and the darkened sky draws upon the sea like drooping lashes upon a weary eye it is time to take away his pen, and let his thoughts sink into the bottom of the deep amid the eternal secret of that silence.

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 24: The night is dark and your slumber is
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
The night is dark and your slumber is deep in the hush of my being.

Wake, O Pain of Love, for I know not how to open the door, and I stand outside.

The hours wait, the stars watch, the wind is still, the silence is heavy in my heart.

Wake, Love, wake! brim my empty cup, and with a breath of song ruffle the night.

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 25: The bird of the morning sings
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
The bird of the morning sings.

Whence has he word of the morning before the morning breaks, and when the dragon night still holds the sky in its cold black coils?

Tell me, bird of the morning, how, through the twofold night of the sky and the leaves, he found his way into your dream, the messenger out of the east?

The world did not believe you when you cried, "The sun is on his way, the night is no more."

O sleeper, awake!

Bare your forehead, waiting for the first blessing of light, and sing with the bird of the morning in glad faith.

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 26: The beggar in me lifted his lean hands
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
The beggar in me lifted his lean hands to the starless sky and cried into night's ear with his hungry voice.

His prayers were to the blind Darkness who lay like a fallen god in a desolate heaven of lost hopes.

The cry of desire eddied round a chasm of despair, a wailing bird circling its empty nest.

But when morning dropped anchor at the rim of the East, the beggar in me leapt and cried:

"Blessed am I that the deaf night denied me—that its coffer was empty."

He cried, "O Life, O Light, you are precious! and precious is the joy that at last has known you!"

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 27: Sanâtan was telling his beads by the Ganges
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
Sanâtan was telling his beads by the Ganges when a Brahmin in rags came to him and said, "Help me, I am poor!"

"My alms-bowl is all that is my own," said Sanâtan, "I have given away everything I had."

"But my lord Shiva came to me in my dreams," said the Brahmin, "and counselled me to come to you."

Sanâtan suddenly remembered he had picked up a stone without price among the pebbles on the river-bank, and thinking that some one might need it hid it in the sands.

He pointed out the spot to the Brahmin, who wondering dug up the stone.

The Brahmin sat on the earth and mused alone till the sun went down behind the trees, and cowherds went home with their cattle.

Then he rose and came slowly to Sanâtan and said, "Master, give me the least fraction of the wealth that disdains all the wealth of the world."

And he threw the precious stone into the water.

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 28: Time after time I came to your gate
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
Time after time I came to your gate with raised hands, asking for more and yet more.

You gave and gave, now in slow measure, now in sudden excess.

I took some, and some things I let drop; some lay heavy on my hands; some I made into playthings and broke them when tired; till the wrecks and the hoard of your gifts grew immense, hiding you, and the ceaseless expectation wore my heart out.

Take, oh take—has now become my cry.

Shatter all from this beggar's bowl: put out this lamp of the importunate watcher: hold my hands, raise me from the still-gathering heap of your gifts into the bare infinity of your uncrowded presence.

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 29: You have set me among those who are
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
You have set me among those who are defeated.

I know it is not for me to win, nor to leave the game.

I shall plunge into the pool although but to sink to the bottom.

I shall play the game of my undoing.

I shall stake all I have and when I lose my last penny I shall stake myself, and then I think I shall have won through my utter defeat.

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 30: A smile of mirth spread over the sky
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
A smile of mirth spread over the sky when you dressed my heart in rags and sent her forth into the road to beg.

She went from door to door, and many a time when her bowl was nearly full she was robbed.

At the end of the weary day she came to your palace gate holding up her pitiful bowl, and you came and took her hand and seated her beside you on your throne.

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 31: "Who among you will take up the duty
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
"Who among you will take up the duty of feeding the hungry?" Lord Buddha asked his followers when famine raged at Shravasti.

Ratnâkar, the banker, hung his head and said, "Much more is needed than all my wealth to feed the hungry."

Jaysen, the chief of the King's army, said, "I would gladly give my life's blood, but there is not enough food in my house."

Dharmapâal, who owned broad acres of land, said with a sigh, "The drought demon has sucked my fields dry.  I know not how to pay King's dues."

Then rose Supriyâ, the mendicant's daughter.

She bowed to all and meekly said, "I will feed the hungry."

"How!"  they cried in surprise.  "How can you hope to fulfil that vow?"

"I am the poorest of you all," said Supriyâ, "that is my strength.  I have my coffer and my store at each of your houses."

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 32: My king was unknown to me
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
My king was unknown to me, therefore when he claimed his tribute I was bold to think I would hide myself leaving my debts unpaid.

I fled and fled behind my day's work and my night's dreams.

But his claims followed me at every breath I drew.

Thus I came to know that I am known to him and no place left which is mine.

Now I wish to lay my all before his feet, and gain the right to my place in his kingdom.

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 33: When I thought I would mould you
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
When I thought I would mould you, an image from my life for men to worship, I brought my dust and desires and all my coloured delusions and dreams.

When I asked you to mould with my life an image from your heart for you to love, you brought your fire and force, and truth, loveliness and peace.

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 34: "Sire," announced the servant to the King
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
"Sire," announced the servant to the King, "the saint Narottam has never deigned to enter your royal temple.

"He is singing God's praise under the trees by the open road. The temple is empty of worshippers.

"They flock round him like bees round the white lotus, leaving the golden jar of honey unheeded."

The King, vexed at heart, went to the spot where Narottam sat on the grass.

He asked him, "Father, why leave my temple of the golden dome and sit on the dust outside to preach God's love?"

"Because God is not there in your temple," said Narottam.

The King frowned and said, "Do you know, twenty millions of gold went to the making of that marvel of art, and it was consecrated to God with costly rites?"

"Yes, I know it," answered Narottam.  "It was in that year when thousands of your people whose houses had been burned stood vainly asking for help at your door.

"And God said, 'The poor creature who can give no shelter to his brothers would build my house!'

"And he took his place with the shelterless under the trees by the road.

"And that golden bubble is empty of all but hot vapour of pride."

The King cried in anger, "Leave my land."

Calmly said the saint, "Yes, banish me where you have banished my God."

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 35: The trumpet lies in the dust
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
The trumpet lies in the dust.

The wind is weary, the light is dead.

Ah, the evil day!

Come, fighters, carrying your flags, and singers, with your war-songs!

Come, pilgrims of the march, hurrying on your journey!

The trumpet lies in the dust waiting for us.

I was on my way to the temple with my evening offerings, seeking for a place of rest after the day's dusty toil: hoping my hurts would be healed and the stains in my garment washed white, when I found thy trumpet lying in the dust.

Was it not the hour for me to light my evening lamp?

Had not the night sung its lullaby to the stars?

O thou blood-red rose, my poppies of sleep have paled and faded!

I was certain my wanderings were over and my debts all paid when suddenly I came upon thy trumpet lying in the dust.

Strike my drowsy heart with thy spell of youth!

Let my joy in life blaze up in fire.  Let the shafts of awakening fly through the heart of night, and a thrill of dread shake blindness and palsy.

I have come to raise thy trumpet from the dust.

Sleep is no more for me—my walk shall be through showers of arrows.

Some shall run out of their houses and come to my side—some shall weep.

Some in their beds shall toss and groan in dire dreams.

For to-night thy trumpet shall be sounded.

From thee I have asked peace only to find shame.

Now I stand before thee—help me to put on my armour!

Let hard blows of trouble strike fire into my life.

Let my heart beat in pain, the drum of thy victory.

My hands shall be utterly emptied to take up thy trumpet.

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 36: When
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text:
When, mad in their mirth, they raised dust to soil thy robe, O Beautiful, it made my heart sick.

I cried to thee and said, "Take thy rod of punishment and judge them."

The morning light struck upon those eyes, red with the revel of night; the place of the white lily greeted their burning breath; the stars through the depth of the sacred dark stared at their carousing—at those that raised dust to soil thy robe, O Beautiful!

Thy judgment seat was in the flower garden, in the birds' notes in springtime: in the shady river-banks, where the trees muttered in answer to the muttering of the waves.

O my Lover, they were pitiless in their passion.

They prowled in the dark to snatch thy ornaments to deck their own desires.

When they had struck thee and thou wert pained, it pierced me to the quick, and I cried to thee and said, "Take thy sword, O my Lover, and judge them!"

Ah, but thy justice was vigilant.

A mother's tears were shed on their insolence; the imperishable faith of a lover hid their spears of rebellion in its own wounds.

Thy judgment was in the mute pain of sleepless love: in the blush of the chaste: in the tears of the night of the desolate: in the pale morning-light of forgiveness.

O Terrible, they in their reckless greed climbed thy gate at night, breaking into thy storehouse to rob thee.

But the weight of their plunder grew immense, too heavy to carry or to remove.

Thereupon I cried to thee and said, Forgive them, O Terrible!

Thy forgiveness burst in storms, throwing them down, scattering their thefts in the dust.

Thy forgiveness was in the thunder-stone; in the shower of blood; in the angry red of the sunset.

poems.title: Fruit-Gathering 37: Upagupta
poems.author: Rabindranath Tagore
poems.text: Upagupta, the disciple of Buddha, lay asleep on the dust by the city wall of Mathura. Lamps were all out, doors were all shut, and stars were all hidden by the murky sky of August. Whose feet were those tinkling with anklets, touching his breast of a sudden? He woke up startled, and the light from a woman's lamp struck his forgiving eyes. It was the dancing girl, starred with jewels, clouded with a pale-blue mantle, drunk with the wine of her youth. She lowered her lamp and saw the young face, austerely beautiful. "Forgive me, young ascetic," said the woman; "graciously come to my house. The dusty earth is not a fit bed for you."
